content: Frameworks have been developed to monitor the healthcare and health system responses to HIV and sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) in both the general population and among people living with HIV. These frameworks recommend specific national-level indicators or actions, and some also provide guidance for global, subnational, and community-level indicators or actions. The Interagency Working Group on SRH and HIV Linkages, along with monitoring and evaluation (M&E) experts from various sectors—including country representatives, donors, UN agencies, and civil society—collaboratively identified and assessed existing indicators and tools. The results of this process were published in the 2014 SRH and HIV Linkages Compendium, which included indicators and related assessment tools. Building on this, the SRHR and HIV Linkages Index was developed, with publication expected in 2017. In collaboration with the M&E teams of the WHO Departments of Reproductive Health and Research (RHR) and HIV, data on countryand regional-level implementation of these recommendations will be collected to evaluate their shortto medium-term impact on national policies in individual WHO Member States. Selected frameworks for monitoring healthcare and health system responses to HIV and SRHR, along with recommended indicators and actions, are detailed in several key publications, including tools for setting and monitoring HIV prevention and treatment targets, strategic information guidelines, and frameworks for gender-sensitive monitoring and evaluation systems. The guideline will be updated five years after publication unless significant new evidence necessitates earlier revision. The WHO Steering Group will monitor research developments in SRHR for women living with HIV, particularly in areas with limited or low-quality evidence, to determine whether new recommendations or changes to existing ones are warranted. Concerns about the validity of any recommendation will be promptly addressed, and plans will be made to update the recommendation as needed. Toward the end of the guideline's five-year validity period, a scoping exercise will be conducted among people living with HIV, technical experts, healthcare professionals, and researchers to identify priority areas requiring further evidence-based guidance. All technical products developed during the guideline's creation, including systematic review reports and search strategies, will be archived for future reference. WHO aims to develop additional guidance on topics that promote equity, are feasible to implement, and contribute to improving SRHR for women living with HIV. These recommendations will be included in future updates of the guideline.
